source.title: Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation
source.authors: Bing-Xi Hou; Guochao Jiang; Guo-Feng Quan; Wei-Qin Li; Wen-Feng Feng; Guo-Hua Liu; Yue-Wei Zhang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper extends policy-shift distillation to mathematical and code reasoning across several student sizes, reporting students' task performance against the teacher and endpoint-only transfer. It does not reproduce Burns et al.'s weak-label training recipe or calculate PGR.
record.gate_note: The paper's own task-performance results are recorded below. It also reports gate diagnostics and training-time and response-length comparisons, which do not measure the weak-to-strong task-performance outcomes in the claim versions. Comparisons to other work mentioned only in related work are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: A smaller Qwen3-4B RL teacher supervises larger Qwen3 students (8B, 14B, 30B-A3B) through policy-shift distillation. The paper reports whether students exceed the supervisor on math and code (Section 5.1, Tables 1, 2, 7), which bears on V1 and V3 in a new setting. Waypoint-OPD versus Direct-OPD under the same supervisor bears on V2. Caveats: supervision is a log-prob policy shift, not weak labels. No strong ceiling is trained, so PGR cannot be computed. The teacher is weak only in size: on the task the Final teacher (56.13) far exceeds every base student (24.84–28.03 math).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that early/late teacher-shift agreement usefully gates the endpoint shift, giving the highest domain average in all six settings, with ablations supporting gating and normalization. They also note larger students can exceed the Final teacher, but they do not frame the work as a weak-to-strong test.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains students using an RL-induced teacher policy shift on student-generated trajectories, gated by agreement between early and late shifts. It does not train on labels produced by a weak model as in the claim's original recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies by domain and student size; the paper reports two math benchmark exceptions to Waypoint-OPD's gains over Direct-OPD. On Qwen3-8B math, gate assignment and batch-scale normalization affect results. Tested Waypoint positions at teacher RL steps 500, 600, and 700 have a reported 0.05-point range in average score.
record.problems: The method and supervision differ from weak-label fine-tuning in the claim, and PGR is not calculated. Results use Qwen3 models and the reported math and code evaluations; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The authors note that the remaining gain over Direct-OPD cannot be assigned entirely to gating because centering and other differences are retained.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports per-benchmark scores for the main methods in Tables 1 and 7; these were not all extracted as separate rows due to the 60-row cap, retaining the domain averages and the two explicitly identified math exceptions. Figure 3's full training trajectories are figure-only; the text-stated step-100 differences are included. Training-time, response-length, and gate-diagnostic results were left out because they do not report the claim's weak-to-strong task-performance outcome.

untested.parts: Training on weak labels; PGR (no strong-ceiling student trained on ground truth).
Auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensembling, loss variants; PGR rather than raw accuracy.
Supervisor size (only one 4B teacher); NLP classification, chess, reward modelling; predictors of PGR.

missing.what: Baseline methods vs the Final teacher. Direct-OPD exceeds the teacher for 14B math (57.61) and for 14B/30B code (56.30, 56.35), but not for 8B or 30B math. Standard OPD is below the teacher except 14B math (56.17).

Per-benchmark teacher comparisons. 14B beats the teacher on all 7 math benchmarks; 14B and 30B beat it on 4 of 5 code evaluations. 8B stays below the teacher on AIME25/26 throughout training but exceeds it on HMMT25N from step 60.
Base student scores before transfer (24.84–28.03 math; 41.03–50.33 code), all below the teacher. This bears on whether the 4B supervisor is 'weak' on the task.

record.verdict_notes: The weak-to-strong reading is indirect. The supervisor is smaller but stronger on the task than every base student. Supervision is an RL policy shift, not labels. With no ceiling, PGR cannot be computed. Waypoint-position rows (r17–r19) and the shuffled-gate control (r14) are own-method diagnostics and are unlinked.

versions.untested_parts: The study transfers RL-induced policy shifts rather than fine-tuning on labels produced by a weaker model, and does not calculate PGR.

It compares Waypoint-OPD with endpoint Direct-OPD and tests gate and normalization ablations, but does not test auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, or the stated loss variants, and does not report PGR.
It reports task performance across student sizes and math/code tasks, not PGR. It does not test NLP tasks, reward modelling, or what predicts PGR.
The study does not test supervisor-checking exploits, distribution shift, or shared teacher-student errors.
No theoretical conditions for a student to beat its supervisor are tested.
No vision or other non-language modality is tested.
